account_fact_cards.title: A setting and reasons for change
account_fact_cards.body: Montgomery bus rules treated Black riders unfairly. These rules had lasted for years. In 1954, the Women’s Political Council asked for fairer bus treatment. Little changed. These grievances gave people reasons to protest.

origin.part: C Unfair bus rules; F Earlier calls for change

account_fact_cards.scope: Background and long-term causes. Existing groups enabled action; their existence is not itself the unfair treatment causing protest.

account_fact_cards.title: An arrest helped set off action
account_fact_cards.body: Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a Montgomery bus. Police arrested her. Organisers then called for people to stay off buses on 5 December. The arrest was a trigger, not the only cause.
account_fact_cards.scope: Trigger is distinct from long-term grievances and the later boycott start.
account_fact_cards.origin_label: Earlier learning: Week 2 context; Week 3 A; Week 4 B.

account_fact_cards.title: Many people sustained the boycott
account_fact_cards.body: The boycott began on 5 December 1955. Many Black residents avoided the buses. They walked or shared rides. Volunteers and local groups raised funds and arranged lifts. Shared effort helped the campaign last.

origin.part: S1 A call to stay off buses; S3 Keeping the protest going
C A protest kept going by many

account_fact_cards.scope: Do not say every participant used a carpool or one leader sustained the campaign alone.

P1 A legal case alongside the protest

hinge.question: Which is the best plan for a historical account? A: List dates but give no reasons. B: Use the five parts, dated evidence, reasons and results, and a limit. C: Write only about one famous person.
hinge.answer_and_decision_rule: B, with a reason. A gives chronology without explanation. C leaves out the campaign’s setting, shared effort and legal route. If needed, model fact plus because and a clear paragraph purpose, then use the parallel check before the own draft.
hinge.parallel: A pupil writes: Parks was arrested, then the boycott began. Does then explain why it began? No. Add that the arrest helped prompt a call to act, while unfair rules and earlier requests were longer causes. Time order needs an explained link.

staff_care_rules: Teach racism factually and calmly. No copied slurs, discriminatory seating, victim simulation, role play or personal disclosure. Do not ask pupils to defend racist rules or imagine being a targeted person. Historical names and dates are allowed; no living private identities or local school details are used.

Agree the quiet signal, usual supervising adult, safe place and return check before starting. Keep all pupils supervised. If the sole adult cannot safely supervise separate spaces, pause the group or offer a calm area in the room while using the normal support route.

Acknowledge distress without probing. Stop the demand and offer the agreed pause without sanction or a public explanation. Follow existing safeguarding arrangements for disclosures. Do not require a catch-up discussion while a pupil is upset.

Stop racist or flippant remarks calmly and firmly, name the harm without repeating a slur, correct the fact and reset respectful language. Check those affected and follow up privately. Use school procedures for repeated, targeted or serious incidents; do not stage a debate about whether racism is valid.
Offer the neutral task and a private check when ready. Record deferred work as not yet evidenced. A pause task or partner’s answer does not establish the history outcome.

Part
What to include
Background
Montgomery, Alabama, USA, 1955–1956; unfair bus rules.
Causes
Long grievances and earlier requests; arrest as a trigger.
Key events
1 December arrest; 5 December boycott; 1956 court case; 20–21 December end and return.

Shared action and legal work mattered. No single-hero account.

Word
Meaning
account
A piece of writing explaining what happened and why it mattered.
background
The setting that helps us understand events.
cause
A reason why something happened.
trigger
An event that helps set off action.
chronology
Events placed in time order.
consequence
An effect or result of an event or action.
significance
How and why something matters in history.
paragraph
A group of sentences about one main part of the account.
connective
A word or phrase that links ideas.
boycott
Not using or buying something as a protest.
segregation
Rules that keep groups apart unfairly.
plaintiff
A person who brings a case to court.
Plan in any language. Because gives a reason; however adds a limit. Dates help the reader follow time order.
